vBRIEFInfo.author: agent:deft-directive-setup
vBRIEFInfo.description: libxumux specification — xumux protocol TypeScript library

narratives.Overview: libxumux is an isomorphic TypeScript library implementing the xumux v0.1.0-draft protocol (https://xumux.org). xumux is a transport-agnostic binary channel multiplexing protocol — a standard way to run multiple typed, named logical channels over a single connection. libxumux exposes a Web Streams (ReadableStream / WritableStream) API and supports all transports in the spec: WebSocket, WebRTC DataChannel, Node.js TCP, stdio, and QUIC/WebTransport. It targets both Node.js and web browsers with no environment-specific APIs leaking across the boundary.
narratives.ProblemStatement: Running multiple independent logical channels over a single transport connection today requires either a custom ad-hoc protocol or accepting a heavy, opinionated framework. The xumux spec defines a minimal, composable binary framing + multiplexing layer that solves exactly this. There is no TypeScript reference implementation, leaving TypeScript/JavaScript developers without a drop-in library to build xumux-based protocols.
narratives.Goals: 1. Implement the full xumux v0.1.0-draft binary frame format and protocol semantics. 2. Support all five spec-defined transports: WebSocket, WebRTC DataChannel, Node.js TCP (net.Socket), Node.js stdio, and QUIC/WebTransport. 3. Run identically in Node.js and modern browsers with no environment-specific code in shared modules. 4. Expose a modern Web Streams (ReadableStream/WritableStream) API so channels compose naturally with the platform I/O model. 5. Implement both client (HELLO initiator) and server (WELCOME responder) roles. 6. Ship as an ESM + CJS dual package built with tsup, with TypeScript declarations.
narratives.UserStories: US-1: As a protocol author, I want to open named channels over a WebSocket so my application protocol does not need to multiplex itself. US-2: As a browser developer, I want a single import that works in both the browser and Node.js so I don't maintain two codepaths. US-3: As a server developer using Node.js, I want to accept xumux connections over TCP and manage channels with a stream-based API. US-4: As a library consumer, I want clear error events when the remote violates the protocol so I can react gracefully. US-5: As a WebRTC application developer, I want to multiplex multiple data streams over a single DataChannel without losing per-channel ordering.
narratives.Requirements: FR-1: Implement 6-byte standard frame encoder (Channel:1, Type:1, Flags:1, Reserved:1, Length:2, Payload). FR-2: Implement 8-byte extended frame encoder/decoder (EXTENDED_LENGTH flag, 4-byte length, max ~4GB payload). FR-3: Implement frame decoder with streaming partial-read support (suitable for TCP/stdio byte streams). FR-4: Implement message fragmentation: split messages exceeding transport MTU into FRAGMENT / FRAGMENT_END frames; enforce single in-flight fragment per channel. FR-5: Implement fragment reassembly: accumulate FRAGMENT frames until FRAGMENT_END, emit complete message; reject interleaved fragments as a protocol error. FR-6: Implement control channel (0x00) message codec for all spec types: HELLO (0x01), WELCOME (0x02), OPEN_CHANNEL (0x03), CHANNEL_ACK (0x04), CLOSE_CHANNEL (0x05), CHANNEL_REJECT (0x06), PING (0x10), PONG (0x11), CLOSE (0x20), ERROR (0xF0). Control plane payloads are JSON/UTF-8. FR-7: Implement client role: send HELLO on transport open, await WELCOME, then enable application channels. FR-8: Implement server role: await HELLO, send WELCOME, manage channel ID assignment. FR-9: Implement dynamic channel lifecycle: OPEN_CHANNEL request, CHANNEL_ACK response, CHANNEL_REJECT on refusal, CLOSE_CHANNEL teardown, channel ID reuse after close. FR-10: Implement keepalive: send PING on configurable interval, expect PONG within timeout, emit error and close on timeout. FR-11: Implement graceful close: send CLOSE (with reason), await CLOSE echo, then close transport. FR-12: Implement magic number (0x4F 0x4D 0x55 0x58 = 'OMUX') write on connect and validate on receive for stream-oriented transports (TCP, stdio); skip for message-oriented transports (WebSocket, WebRTC, QUIC). FR-13: Implement WebSocket transport adapter — works in browser (native WebSocket) and Node.js (ws package or native). FR-14: Implement WebRTC DataChannel transport adapter — browser and Node.js (node-datachannel or wrtc). FR-15: Implement Node.js TCP transport adapter (net.Socket). FR-16: Implement Node.js stdio transport adapter (process.stdin/stdout). FR-17: Implement QUIC/WebTransport transport adapter. FR-18: Expose each open channel as a { readable: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>, writable: WritableStream<Uint8Array> } pair. FR-19: Surface non-fatal protocol errors as 'error' events on the connection object; surface fatal errors (bad magic, version mismatch) as thrown exceptions / rejected promises that also close the connection. NFR-1: All shared code (codec, control, channel) MUST contain zero Node.js-specific API calls (no Buffer, no net, no process) — browser-safe by construction. NFR-2: TypeScript strict mode enabled; zero any types in public API surface. NFR-3: ESM + CJS dual package output via tsup; exports map in package.json. NFR-4: Tree-shakeable: transport adapters are side-effect-free separate entry points so bundlers can exclude unused transports. NFR-5: Zero mandatory runtime dependencies in the shared core; transport adapters may have optional peer dependencies. NFR-6: >= 85% line/branch coverage via Vitest. NFR-7: All public API types exported and documented with JSDoc.
narratives.SuccessMetrics: 1. All xumux v0.1.0-draft MUST-level requirements satisfied (verified by conformance tests mirroring spec language). 2. Full round-trip test: client connects over WebSocket, opens two channels, sends fragmented messages on both, closes gracefully — passes in both Node.js and browser (Vitest + Playwright). 3. >= 85% Vitest coverage across codec, control, and connection modules. 4. package size: ESM bundle imports < 50 KB uncompressed (excluding transport adapters). 5. TypeScript consumers get full type inference with zero 'any' in the public API.
narratives.Architecture: src/codec/ — Pure binary frame encoder and decoder. encode-frame.ts: builds Uint8Array for standard and extended frames. decode-frame.ts: streaming state machine that reads header then payload; handles partial reads for TCP/stdio. fragment.ts: fragmentor (splits large messages) and reassembler (accumulates FRAGMENT frames, emits on FRAGMENT_END). No Node.js APIs here. src/control/ — Control channel message codec. messages.ts: typed interfaces for all 10 control message types. codec.ts: JSON serialise/deserialise control payloads. handler.ts: dispatches incoming control frames to lifecycle state machine. src/channel.ts — Channel abstraction. Wraps a { readable: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>, writable: WritableStream<Uint8Array> } pair. Tracks channel state (opening, open, closing, closed). src/connection.ts — Connection lifecycle. XumuxClient: initiates HELLO, manages channel table, dispatches frames. XumuxServer: awaits HELLO, sends WELCOME, manages server-side channel table. Both extend a shared XumuxPeer base class. Keepalive timer lives here. src/transports/ — Transport adapters. Each adapter implements a TransportAdapter interface: { send(data: Uint8Array): void, receive(): AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>, close(): void }. websocket-adapter.ts: wraps native WebSocket (browser) or ws (Node.js); no magic bytes. webrtc-adapter.ts: wraps RTCDataChannel; no magic bytes. tcp-adapter.ts: Node.js net.Socket; writes OMUX magic on connect, validates on receive. stdio-adapter.ts: process.stdin/stdout; writes OMUX magic, validates on receive. quic-adapter.ts: WebTransport stream; no magic bytes. src/index.ts — Re-exports XumuxClient, XumuxServer, and all transport adapters. Transport adapters are also available as separate deep imports (libxumux/transports/websocket) so bundlers can tree-shake unused ones. Build: tsup with two entry points (src/index.ts + src/transports/*); outputs dist/esm/ and dist/cjs/; generates .d.ts. Testing: Vitest; in-memory transport adapter for unit tests; browser tests via Playwright + Vitest browser mode.
